Accepted as a complete faithful refutation, as declared in the record and Challenge docstring; the positive printed theorem is not being certified. Choose delta=0,r=1/4,A=1/2 and alpha=1/2. For every n>=2, the power-mean inequality gives fourthNorm(v)>=sqrt((n-1)/n)*sqrt(popVar(w)); since sqrt((n-1)/n)>1/2, Theta forces both arm potential arrays w to be constant. At the LATE their population means coincide, so every observed adjusted-response array is constant, the AR statistic is zero, and coverage is 1. For every real beta and n>=2 the class contains the all-complier model y(0)=0,y(1)=beta with n1=floor(n/2). Thus both nested infima equal 1 on nonempty classes and the asserted limit 1-alpha fails. scratch/Checks.lean also compiles a member of this small-A class.

Accepted as a complete faithful refutation. Fix k=1,delta=0,e=1/4,A=4,B=1/2,r=1/4 and alpha=1/2. The same power-mean inequality, using the OLS intercept normal equation, forces both population residual arrays to be zero for n>=2. Under the fixed covariate moment and eigenvalue bounds, the probability of a fixed-threshold deviation in either arm's first or second covariate moment is O(1/n), uniformly in the model, by the finite-population variance bound; consequently either arm being singular has probability O(1/n). On every full-rank assignment both observed arm responses fit their population affine functions exactly, the intercepts coincide at the LATE, adjustedTau=0, and the assignment is accepted. Therefore the infimum of coverage tends to 1. These classes are nonempty for every beta and all sufficiently large n: take all compliers, y(0)=0,y(1)=beta, centered equally spaced x in [-1,1], and n1=floor(n/2). The covariate second moment is at least 1/3, its fourth moment is at most 1, and the residuals vanish. scratch/Checks.lean compiles a concrete Xi member with these constants. This argument does not rely on an empty infimum or on a singular-matrix zero fallback.
